objects.definition:
enum ExitCode {
    Success = 0,
    GeneralFailure = 32,
    NetworkFailure = 33,
    TimeoutFailure = 34,
    NotIndexed = 35,
    ConnectionFailure = 36,
    ProtocolFailure = 37,
    ArgumentParseError = 38,
    UnexpectedMessageError = 39,
    UnknownMessageError = 40
};
objects.description: Exit/status codes used by RTags tooling to report outcome categories such as success, failures, and protocol errors.
Indicates the language mode of a compilation unit (C or C++).
High-level categorization of libclang cursor kinds used by RTags.
Bitflags controlling how a cursor is converted to a string for logging or diagnostics.
RAII wrapper around a libclang CXTranslationUnit and its CXIndex, providing creation, loading, visiting, reparsing, and automatic disposal.
Flags to customize TranslationUnit creation behavior, e.g., display diagnostics or adjust include handling.
Helper base to construct Location objects from libclang locations, normalizing paths and filtering built-ins; requires subclass to map a Path/line/col to a Location.

Abstract provider for diagnostics across one or more CXTranslationUnits. Supplies helpers to convert libclang locations to project Locations and to iterate diagnostics. Subclasses implement data access.
Holds a cursor and its resolved CXType for cases where 'auto' needs explicit resolution.
Matcher utility to filter libclang cursors by kind, name, and argument count, with AND/OR combination modes.
Comparable wrapper for a symbol, storing its Location, definition state, and kind, with a ranking to prioritize items during sorting.
Selects whether to search for a project root relative to source tree or build tree.
Bitflags controlling behavior of findAncestor when searching directories up the tree.
Caches various filesystem-derived data to speed up project operations: parsed rtags config by path, compiler resolution, and ancestor directory lookups with flags-aware keys.
RAII helper to manage a CXString's lifetime, automatically disposing it on destruction and providing convenience accessors and comparisons.
